title: Latent Space Collapse? Understanding the Effects of Narrow Fine-Tuning on LLMs
primary_claim: Narrow sentiment fine-tuning of GPT-2 does not simply overwrite pretrained representations but reconfigures and 'squishes' the model's output and activation space, concentrating sentiment information in middle-to-late layers while sharply degrading general language modeling (perplexity) on non-sentiment inputs.
quote: fine-tuning does not simply overwrite pre-trained representations but reconfigures them entirely, redistributing sentiment-specific information across layers and squishing the output representation space
tolerance_rationale: other scalar metric: 15% relative; post reported no spread, tolerance is a guess

needed: imdb (HF datasets, for sentiment fine-tuning and eval)

inspector_notes: Clean, small-scale, fully self-contained notebook sequence (finetune -> post-finetune analysis -> logit-lens perplexity/entropy -> alignment/transferability). No README beyond a one-paragraph pointer to the LessWrong post; no requirements file, but all dependencies are standard and unpinned so version drift risk is low for such a simple pipeline.
headline_artifact: compute_perplexity() output in logit-lens-analysis.ipynb comparing base vs. fine-tuned GPT-2 on non-sentiment text (the 160.87 vs 49,802.45 numbers).

extension.what_varies: the package resolution date only: uv pip install --exclude-newer <post date + 14 d> (2025-03-14); if the same kwarg failure persists, step back to 2024-10-15 and record the offset. Code, notebooks, data, hardware unchanged.
extension.rationale: parent ledgered env (TrainingArguments evaluation_strategy removed mid-4.x). Tests whether undoing rot yields a reproduction (headline 160.87 vs 49802 mean pairwise distance) or exposes fragility; the freeze-date offset needed is a measure of rot age at publication.
